title: Verb-centric admin audit taxonomy and event envelope for SSO/RBAC v2
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Proposal for a verb-centric admin audit taxonomy and a single JSON envelope (event envelope) that captures SSO/SAML assertions, actor provenance, target attribution, and a compact field-patch format optimized for high-cardinality admin ops. Focus: what to log (minimum required attributes), how to represent actor/target, safe redaction rules, sampling & retention tiers, and query indexes for forensic and compliance use cases.
acceptance_criteria: Audit event envelope defined and documented in Confluence with examples for common admin flows
Event payloads contain required actor/target/correlation fields and conform to size limits (<16KB default)
Redaction guidelines published and unit-tested in the audit canonicalizer service
Storage mapping and Elasticsearch/Kafka indexing keys agreed (actor_id, target_id, correlation_id, event_class, timestamp)
Migration plan for 90-day backfill of critical events and sampling policy implemented in ingestion pipeline
notes: This ticket prioritizes long-term forensic usefulness over ultra-compact payloads; we balance by allowing sampled verbose payloads and compact summaries for bulk events.
We avoid exposing raw SAML attributes in plaintext; recommend attribute-level allowlist and redaction rules for PII-sensitive attributes (email partial mask, phone hash).
We propose a layered retention model: full payload (90 days for high-risk admin actions), summary (365 days), and index-only (7 years for compliance queries).
Correlation strategy: every UI/CLI/API admin operation MUST include request_id and actor_session_id; SSO flows MUST attach assertion_id and idp_entity_id when available.
comments: 2025-11-12 - Diego: Initial draft reviewed; suggested adding verb-level taxonomy (e.g., grant, revoke, escalate, rollback) instead of generic 'mutate' labels.
2025-12-02 - Priya (Security): Recommend adding HSM/KMS key reference hashing pattern for crypto operations and explicit 'crypto_use' event_class.

implementation_outline: 1) Define envelope and verb taxonomy; 2) Implement canonicalizer changes to populate actor provenance and SAML metadata; 3) Add field-patch encoder in ingestion; 4) Update storage mapping and indices; 5) Add redaction and sampling hooks; 6) Rollout and backfill plan.
query_index_strategy: Primary index: timestamp + event_class + correlation_id; Secondary: actor_id, target_id, assertion_id. Use time-partitioned indices (daily) and a separate cold store for full payloads older than 90 days.
redaction_rules: 1) PII attributes in SAML (email, phone) must be masked unless allowlisted by compliance; 2) Secrets/keys never logged in plaintext; replace with key_hash; 3) Use attribute allowlist per event_class; 4) Provide per-customer redaction overrides for Private deployments.
sampling_policy: High-volume non-privileged audit classes (e.g., read.list_users) default to summary-only at 1% sample; all privileged verbs (grant,revoke,escalate,login-fail,credential-rotation) are always logged full. Sampling applied at ingestion boundary with sampled_reason tag.
migration_and_backfill: Phase A: start writing new envelope in parallel (dual-write) for 4 weeks. Phase B: run backfill for high-priority events (permission.* and policy.*) for last 90 days using transform job. Phase C: decommission old schema after verification.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Canary in staging with traffic mirroring. Stage 2: 10% of production writes for 48h. Stage 3: 100% write with retention policy enforcement. Post-rollout: run weekly sanity checks for 30 days.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Event size spikes causing ingestion throttles. Mitigation: enforce 16KB default payload cap and provide archive link for oversized payloads.
Risk: PII leakage from SAML attributes. Mitigation: attribute allowlist + automated redaction + security review gating for any new logged attributes.
Risk: Index cost growth. Mitigation: time-partitioned indices, summary-only retention for low-risk classes, and tiered cold storage.
